subject: SKU consolidation + discount appendix — proposed orderform redlines
messages:
From: Janelle Park <janelle.park@skylinehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@skylinehealth.com
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing appendix + SKU consolidation (RFP follow-up)

Hi Mina —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Per our procurement team’s ask, I attached Skyline’s pricing template and a proposed SKU list we want to collapse into three metered lines for simplicity (attached: Skyline_RFP_Pricing_Template.xlsx).

Two quick asks from procurement:
- Can Redwood map the proposed consolidated SKUs to the orderform pricing appendix with a clear definition for each meter?
- We need explicit language for temporary onboarding credits (one-time) vs. permanent commit floors. Procurement is sensitive to any floor that could lock us into a minimum annual spend without true-up.

Can you confirm whether the cap/floor language in the draft orderform (we received SKY_OrderForm_Draft_v2.pdf) can be modified to show: (a) a one-time onboarding credit instead of lowering the fee floor, and (b) a 12-month true-up window for usage-based metrics?

Appreciate quick visibility — procurement has an internal deadline Friday.

Best,
Janelle Park
Director, Strategic Sourcing
Skyline Health

Attachments: Skyline_RFP_Pricing_Template.xlsx (Excel), draft map: pricing-appendix-sku-map.csv (CSV)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Janelle Park <janelle.park@skylinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing appendix + SKU consolidation (RFP follow-up)

Thanks Janelle — and thanks for sending the template.

Short answers up front: yes, we can map the consolidated SKUs into the pricing appendix and we prefer a one-time onboarding credit over changing the permanent fee floor. We also agree a 12-month true-up window is reasonable.

Next steps from our side:
- I attached an initial SKU mapping (pricing-appendix-sku-map.csv) that maps Skyline’s suggested buckets to Redwood meters and shows estimated token ranges per bucket.
- Marissa, can you propose the commercial concession (one-time onboarding credit amount) and confirm this stays outside the committed-floor calculation?
- Karthik, legal will you propose redline language that: (1) makes the onboarding credit a one-time, non-recurring credit; (2) preserves Redwood’s standard minimum-commit true-up but constrains any floor not to be reduced as part of this credit; and (3) adds a 12-month reconciliation / true-up clause?
- Laura, finance — please flag any revenue recognition or billing timing concerns if we accept a one-time credit that offsets first quarter invoices.

If we can get legal/finance redlines today, Marissa will deliver a customer-facing summary to Janelle by EOD. Otherwise we’ll aim for first thing Thu morning so procurement can hit their Friday deadline.

Mina Haddad
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing-appendix-sku-map.csv (CSV)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing appendix + SKU consolidation (RFP follow-up)

Mina —

Reviewed the draft orderform (SKY_OrderForm_Draft_v2.pdf) and the SKU map. High level legal takeaways and proposed redlines below. I’ve pasted the suggested language snippets for insertion into Exhibit B (Pricing Appendix) and the Order Form definitions.

1) Onboarding credit (one-time)
- Proposed language (for Exhibit B): "Customer will receive a one-time onboarding credit in the amount specified on the Order Form. Such credit is non-recurring, applied to the first invoice(s) following the Effective Date, and does not alter or reduce any Minimum Commit or Fee Floor set forth in this Agreement."

2) Fee Floor / Minimum Commit
- We should avoid a permanent reduction to the fee floor. Instead: add a carve-out that explicitly states the onboarding credit shall not be treated as a reduction of Customer's minimum committed spend for any Contract Year.
- Proposed language (Definitions): add definition of "Onboarding Credit" and cross-reference in "Minimum Commit" clause.

3) True-up window and reconciliation
- We can accept a 12-month reconciliation period for usage true-up; include specifics: Redwood will perform an annual reconciliation within 60 days following each Contract Year, with a final settlement invoice if usage exceeds committed levels, or a credit to future invoices if usage materially underperformed (subject to anti-abuse language).

4) SKU consolidation mapping and meter definitions
- Technical teams should sign off on meter definitions in Exhibit B. Legal will flag any ambiguous definitions that could alter billable units (e.g., what constitutes a "session" vs. a "token-bucket"). Recommend we add a short bullet list in Exhibit B defining the mapping and attach the CSV as non-normative Appendix A for clarity.

5) Cap on discounting / promotional credits
- If procurement requests a permanent lower floor or additional recurring discount tier tied to volume bands, we should limit permanent discounting to explicit commit bands only, and model economic impact. For this deal I recommend offering a one-time onboarding credit up to $50k as a concession (commercial to confirm), rather than lowering the floor.

If the team agrees I will prepare the redline to the Order Form removing language that treats credits as floor reductions and add the reconciliation clause.

-Karthik
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Hi Janelle —

Following internal review (legal + finance), Redwood can accept the SKU consolidation and will provide the customer-side appendix with explicit meter definitions. Per Karthik’s suggested language, we will: (a) issue a one-time onboarding credit (we are proposing $45,000), (b) add language clarifying the credit is non-recurring and does not reduce the Minimum Commit, and (c) include a 12-month reconciliation clause in the Pricing Appendix.

Proposed commercial summary for procurement:
- One-time onboarding credit: $45,000 applied to first two invoices (non-recurring).
- No permanent reduction to the fee floor; Minimum Commit stays as stated in the Order Form.
- Annual reconciliation: Redwood will reconcile usage vs. commit within 60 days after the Contract Year; adjustments will be invoiced/credited per reconciliation.
- Exhibit B will include Appendix A (SKU mapping CSV) as a non-normative reference and explicit meter definitions.

If Skyline is comfortable, we’ll prepare a clean redline of the Order Form for signature. Let us know if procurement needs the concession to be structured differently (e.g., percentage discount instead of fixed credit) — we can model both quickly.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this quarter.

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
